card.title: PlayStation 4 WLOD (White Light Of Death) & HDMI Encoder Diagnosis

claims.statement: The HDMI encoder IC is the most common cause of no picture or White Light Of Death (WLOD) and often cannot be diagnosed via standard diode readings.
claims.evidence: Experience shows encoder failure presents with normal diode measurements but no display.
claims.quote: Most common fault is a bad HDMI encoder IC is bad most of the time you can’t measure any faults by reading diode measurements

claims.statement: Check HDMI filter continuity and inspect for shorted capacitors or diodes near the HDMI circuit.
claims.evidence: Damaged filters or shorted components around the encoder cause display failures.
claims.quote: Check continuity filters ... Check diodes and capacitors near the HDMI circuit

claims.statement: If a replaced HDMI encoder IC still results in WLOD, replace the encoder IC again as it may be defective from the factory.
claims.evidence: Factory defects in replacement encoder ICs can perpetuate the fault.
claims.quote: If you replaced encoder IC and still you get a WLOD replace encoder IC again it could be broken from factory.

procedure: Check the hard drive by connecting to a PC.
Inspect the physical state of the HDMI connector and filters.
Check diode and capacitor measurements near the HDMI circuit.
Replace the HDMI encoder IC if no other fault is found.
card.caveats: Diode mode measurements on a bad HDMI encoder can read completely normal.
